The RAS shells were fabricated into 'C' and 'U' shapes.
The absorbing layer is made of glass fiber/epoxy/carbon-black (5 wt%).
The reflection layer is made of carbon fiber/epoxy.
Sixteen plies of glass fiber/epoxy/carbon-black prepreg were used at the bottom.
Eight plies of carbon fiber/epoxy prepreg were used on top.
The RAS shells were cured in an autoclave for 2 hours at 120°C and 5.5 atm pressure.
Spring-back was compensated using aluminum molds with additional bending angles.
The average radar absorption efficiency of the hybrid RAS shells is 11 dB.
The RCS was measured using the compact range method at 10 GHz.
The RCS was predicted using the physical optic (PO) method.
The reflection coefficient of the carbon fiber/epoxy material is about 120 dB, which is considered a perfect electric conductor (PEC).
The mechanical and thermal properties used in the finite element analysis include elastic modulus, Poisson's ratio, and coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE).
The predicted RCS values matched the experimental results with an error of 6.3% for the 'C' shape and 3.5% for the 'U' shape.
The study highlights the need for further research to apply the hybrid RAS to complex military structures and severe environmental conditions.
